title: Bank of Japan MPM decision (MPM Jun 10-11, 2027 — no Outlook Report; the second of Q2 2027's two venues)
source: EST: boj.or.jp 'Monetary Policy Meetings' schedule page (en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 41,959 bytes) and column-parsed out of the HTML by this session independently of the fetches that seeded the sibling BoJ entries. The page carries two tables; the 'Table : 2027' fourth row parses as ['June 10 (Thurs.), 11 (Fri.)', '-', 'June 21 (Mon.)', 'July 27 (Tues.)'] against the header 'Date of MPM | Outlook Report (The Bank's View) | Summary of Opinions | MPM Minutes'. The '-' is the primary evidence that this is NOT an Outlook Report meeting. The decision publishes at the meeting's conclusion on the second day. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the sibling BoJ entries: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: and no slot for any other central bank, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and a schedule published ~21 months ahead is the most movable kind
notes: Proposed during the boj-decision-2027-04-28 initial research (2026-09-05) for two reasons the sibling entries do not cover. FIRST, it is the second of the only TWO MPMs inside Q2 2027 (with Apr 27-28, same primary table) — the window Reuters' 2026-07-23 poll found '70% of economists anticipate the BoJ to hike rates to at least 1.50%' in. The policy rate is 1.0% as of the 2026-06-16 change (k260616a.pdf, 'Change in the Guideline for Money Market Operations', 7-1), so that consensus is two more hikes against seven venues before April 2027; if they land earlier, Q2 2027 is a beyond-terminal window rather than a reaching-terminal one (51% of the same poll called 1.50% the terminal rate). SECOND, and specific to this venue: it is the first MPM able to see a NATIONAL post-tax-cut CPI print. Japan's food consumption-tax cut takes effect 2027-04-01 (japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01, estimate, pending Diet passage); the Apr 27-28 Outlook meeting must therefore project a fiscal year carrying the cut BEFORE any national print covering it exists, while the national April CPI releases roughly three weeks after that meeting. CAUTION ON THAT SECOND POINT: the Statistics Bureau's release schedule (stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html) publishes rows only through the February 2027 survey month (released 2027-03-19), so the April 2027 CPI date is NOT sourced and no CPI event is proposed alongside this one — the claim here is only the ordering that follows from the national print always trailing its survey month, not a date. Third, non-obvious: this is an ORDINARY meeting, and the boj-decision-2027-04-28 ledger measures that on a complete 2025-2026 window the Bank changed the guideline at 1 of 7 Outlook meetings versus 2 of 6 ordinary ones (n=3 changes, thin) — so on this cycle's own record the ordinary June venue is not the less likely of the pair. SAME CHANNEL CAVEAT AS THE OTHER BoJ ENTRIES: yen funding and global term premium are second-order for a US equity book and already owned by the FOMC ledgers; symbols is empty and no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed. This meeting's Summary of Opinions publishes 2027-06-21 and its Minutes 2027-07-27. Estimate widens caution only. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/boj-decision-2027-06-11.md), on three points. ONE, COUNT CORRECTION: the 'seven venues before April 2027' above is one too many — off the same primary schedule table, five decisions stand in front of 2027-04-28 (2026-09-18, 10-30, 12-18, 2027-01-22, 03-18; April is the sixth from 2026-09-05) and six stand in front of this event, which is the seventh. Direction matters slightly: fewer venues means marginally less room for the two hikes, weakening rather than strengthening the beyond-terminal read. TWO, THE DEADLINE FRAMING SUPERSEDES 'the second of two': Q2 2027 holds exactly two MPMs, so this is the LAST venue inside the Reuters poll's window and the meeting at which the 'at least 1.50% in Q2 2027' consensus is adjudicated — registered as FT-boj-decision-2027-06-11-1. THREE, THE CPI ORDERING RUNS SHARPER THAN STATED: projecting the Statistics Bureau's sourced 2026 cadence (national CPI for month M releases ~3 weeks into M+1, Tokyo's flash for M at the end of M), the Apr 27-28 Outlook meeting holds ZERO post-cut CPI readings (Tokyo's April flash lands ~2 days after it) while this meeting holds roughly three and cannot hold the national May print. Still an ordering and not a date — the schedule page was re-fetched 2026-09-05 at the same 13,839 bytes and same 'Last Update : 23 January 2026' stamp, rows still stopping at survey month February 2027.
